title: Bounded-below filtered Hom continuity for stratified dualizable condensed sheaves
statement:
Let $Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and put $B=p_Y^*\Lambda$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(B)$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with ordinary relative derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $K\in D(B)$ admit a finite stratification of $Y$ by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-constructible-subset], on each of which its derived restriction is dualizable: there are an object $D$ and evaluation $D\otimes K\to B$ and coevaluation $B\to K\otimes D$ with the two contraction composites equal to the identities, using the usual associators and unitors [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. Let $I$ be a small filtered category [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], let $C:I\to\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{Mod}_B)$ be a diagram of integer-indexed cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and suppose one integer $a$ satisfies $C_i^j=0$ for every $i$ and $j<a$. Write $C_\infty=\varinjlim_i C_i$ for the termwise sheaf-module colimit with legs $\iota_i$, and $Q$ for passage to $D(B)$. For every integer $r$, the canonical map
$$\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(K,QC_i[r])\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(K,QC_\infty[r]),\qquad [u_i]\longmapsto Q(\iota_i)[r]\circ u_i,$$
is an isomorphism of $\Gamma(*,\Lambda)$-modules. It is natural in $K$ and in morphisms of diagrams. The $C_i$ need not be constructible; no Noetherian or finite-dimensional hypothesis on $Y$ is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(2) and its final global-Hom assertion, passed to cohomology in degree r; strict uniformly bounded-below diagrams are a specialization

proof.text: Put $H_T(A,N)=R\mathcal Hom_{B_T}(A,N)$ and use its functorial complex models. All colimits of such models in this proof are termwise sheaf colimits, not assertions of a colimit universal property in the ordinary derived category. By [lem-sfb-rhom-colimit-cohomology-ladder], their cohomology is the filtered colimit of cohomology; hence they preserve quasi-isomorphisms and common cohomological lower bounds. In particular, a diagram with cohomology zero below $c$ can be replaced functorially by its good truncations in degrees at least $c$ without changing its derived objects or the derived object of its termwise colimit. The truncation projection and the colimit cocone give these identifications, so they retain the original comparison maps. We shall prove internal-Hom continuity for every uniformly cohomologically bounded-below diagram, which includes the strict diagrams in the question.

source.place: Lemma 5.3, proof: t-exactness of filtered colimits and reduction to bounded-below models

proof.text: Apply [lem-fix-constructible-open-closed-refinement] to the given finite constructible partition. It gives a finite binary tree with root $Y$, qcqs vertices, complementary quasi-compact open and closed children, and actual morphisms from its nonempty leaves to original strata over $Y$. By [lem-zl-condensed-lisse-proetale-locality], $K$ restricts to a dualizable object on each leaf. More generally its restriction $K_T$ to any vertex $T$ remains stratified dualizable: intersect the original immersed strata scheme-theoretically with $T$; these form a finite locally closed partition, and their images are constructible by [lem-pur-scheme-constructible-preimage]. Apply the same pullback theorem to their dual pairs. Consequently [lem-pod-stratified-dualizable-bounded] gives an upper cohomological bound $b_T$ for every $K_T$. We prove the stronger internal-Hom assertion by induction up this finite tree; the empty scheme contributes the zero category.

For a dualizable source $A$ on a leaf $T$, let $D$ be its dual. The closed structure of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] identifies $H_T(A,N)$ with $D\otimes^L N$. Explicitly a map $g:V\otimes A\to N$ is sent to $V\to V\otimes A\otimes D\xrightarrow{g\otimes1}N\otimes D\cong D\otimes N$, with the first arrow induced by coevaluation. The inverse tensors a map $V\to D\otimes N$ with $A$, reorders the factors, and applies evaluation $D\otimes A\to B_T$. The two composites cancel by the two triangle identities. These formulas are natural in $V,N$, so the tensor--Hom adjunction identifies the representing objects and their maps in $N$.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(2), lisse case: internal Hom is tensor with the dual

proof.text: Choose a K-flat complex $P$ representing $D$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; then $D\otimes^L N$ is $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes N)$ for every complex $N$. Fix $q$. Under the identification of [lem-sfb-rhom-colimit-cohomology-ladder], $H^q$ of the comparison for $A$ is the colimit of the maps $H^qH_T(A,\iota_s)$ given by the cocone legs, so it depends only on these derived maps. By naturality in $N$ of Step 3 it becomes $\varinjlim_sH^q\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes N_s)\to H^q\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes N_\infty)$, induced by $1_P\otimes\iota_s$. This is bijective: [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor] (after the signed swap of factors) gives $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes N_\infty)\cong\varinjlim_s\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes N_s)$ through these legs, and Step 1 moves $H^q$ past the colimit. By [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] the comparison is invertible: this is internal-Hom continuity on every leaf. For every vertex source $K_T$, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-internal-hom-lower-bound] and Step 2 give $H_T(K_T,N)\in D^{\ge c-b_T}$ for $N\in D^{\ge c}$, uniformly.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(2), dualizable case; proof of the final global-Hom assertion

proof.text: At an internal vertex write $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$. We first establish continuity of $Ri^!$ on diagrams $(N_s)$ with common bound $c$. Use the natural triangle $i_*Ri^!N_s\to N_s\to Rj_*j^*N_s$ of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement]. In its long exact cohomology sequence, take filtered colimits. The rows stay exact by [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor], and Step 1 identifies their terms with the cohomology of the termwise colimits. Compare with the sequence for $N_\infty$. The squares including connecting maps commute by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-ladder]. The middle comparisons are identities; the $Rj_*j^*$ comparisons are isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qcqs-pushforward-continuity], since $j$ is qcqs and $j^*$ is exact and preserves colimits. The five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma], on the segment $H^{q-1}(N)\to H^{q-1}(Rj_*j^*N)\to H^q(i_*Ri^!N)\to H^q(N)\to H^q(Rj_*j^*N)$, gives an isomorphism on the remaining term for every $q$.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(2), final sentences: the support triangle and part (1) for the open immersion

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], $i_*$ is exact and preserves filtered colimits on the qcqs vertex $T$. Thus the remaining comparisons in Step 5 are $i_*$ of the cohomology comparisons for $Ri^!$. By [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement], $i^*i_*\cong1$ and $i^*$ is exact, so they are isomorphisms already on $Z$. This proves the desired costalk comparison, with precisely the maps induced by $Ri^!$ on the cocone. The same recollement statement gives $Ri^!N_s\in D^{\ge c}$, uniformly in $s$. Good truncations as in Step 1 therefore give a strict lower-bounded complex diagram representing these costalks, with termwise colimit representing $Ri^!N_\infty$.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(2), continuity and left t-exactness of closed exceptional restriction

proof.text: Assume internal-Hom continuity is known for $K_U$ and $K_Z$ for all uniformly cohomologically bounded-below diagrams. The first formula of [lem-sfb-open-closed-internal-hom-formulas] gives $H_T(j_!K_U,N)=Rj_*H_U(K_U,j^*N)$. Since $j^*$ is exact and preserves colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement], the induction hypothesis identifies the colimit of the inner Hom diagram with $H_U(K_U,j^*N_\infty)$. Its terms have common lower bound $c-b_U$ by Step 4. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qcqs-pushforward-continuity] to $j$ and that diagram (using good truncations from Step 1) to move $Rj_*$ past this colimit. Hence the canonical internal-Hom comparison is invertible for the source $j_!K_U$. All identifications are natural in $N$ and are the evaluation/adjunction comparisons specified by the formula, so the comparison obtained is the original cocone comparison.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(2), adjunction calculation for extension from an open stratum

proof.text: The second formula of [lem-sfb-open-closed-internal-hom-formulas] gives $H_T(i_*K_Z,N)=i_*H_Z(K_Z,Ri^!N)$. By Steps 5--6 the costalk diagram has common lower bound $c$ and its termwise derived colimit is $Ri^!N_\infty$. Apply the induction hypothesis on $Z$ to its good-truncated representatives. This identifies the colimit of $H_Z(K_Z,Ri^!N_s)$ with $H_Z(K_Z,Ri^!N_\infty)$. Exactness and filtered-colimit preservation of $i_*$ in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] carry this isomorphism to $T$. Thus internal-Hom continuity holds for $i_*K_Z$, again for the canonical comparison, by naturality of the formula.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(2), adjunction calculation for extension from a closed stratum

proof.text: The other localization triangle in [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement] is $j_!K_U\to K_T\to i_*K_Z\to j_!K_U[1]$. For any target diagram as above, [lem-sfb-rhom-colimit-cohomology-ladder] supplies the commuting exact ladder for its three source comparisons, including the connecting squares. Steps 7--8 give the outer isomorphisms in every degree. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] to the segment with terms $H^{q-1}H_T(j_!K_U,-)$, $H^qH_T(i_*K_Z,-)$, $H^qH_T(K_T,-)$, $H^qH_T(j_!K_U,-)$, $H^{q+1}H_T(i_*K_Z,-)$. Then the middle comparison is an isomorphism in every degree, hence in the derived category by [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology]. This completes the finite tree induction and proves internal-Hom continuity for $K$ on $Y$.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(2), induction using the localization triangle

proof.text:
Choose an upper cohomological bound $b$ for $K$ by [lem-pod-stratified-dualizable-bounded]. Then $H_Y(K,QC_i)$ has common lower bound $a-b$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-internal-hom-lower-bound]. Apply the global-sections assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qcqs-pushforward-continuity] on the qcqs scheme $Y$ to good-truncated functorial representatives of this diagram. Step 9 identifies their termwise derived colimit with $H_Y(K,QC_\infty)$, so for every $r$ it gives
$$\varinjlim_i H^rR\Gamma(Y,H_Y(K,QC_i))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^rR\Gamma(Y,H_Y(K,QC_\infty)).$$
By [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] applied to $QC_i[r]$ and [lem-pur-derived-internal-hom-shift-right], these groups are $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(K,QC_i[r])$ and the corresponding group at infinity. The identifications are natural in the target and shift; the resulting leg is therefore exactly $u_i\mapsto Q(\iota_i)[r]\circ u_i$.

source.place: Lemma 5.3, final global-Hom assertion and its proof using the boundedness of constructibles

proof.text: Each comparison just used is induced by the target cocone and evaluation, so is contravariantly natural in $K$ and covariantly natural in diagram morphisms. Explicitly, precomposing $u_i$ with $v:K'\to K$ gives $Q(\iota_i)[r]u_iv=(Q(\iota_i)[r]u_i)v$; for a diagram map $f:C\to C'$ its colimit map satisfies $f_\infty\iota_i=\iota'_if_i$, which is the required target square after applying $Q$ and shift. Scalar multiplication by $s\in\Gamma(*,\Lambda)$ is the central action of its pulled-back coefficient section on module maps. Composition with $Q(\iota_i)[r]$ commutes with that action, so the bijection of abelian groups is linear over $\Gamma(*,\Lambda)$ and hence an isomorphism of modules. This also covers zero objects, empty $Y$, and arbitrary integer shifts.

source.place: Lemma 5.3, canonical global-Hom comparison: scalar linearity and naturality

proof_origin.place: Lemma 5.3(2), its proof on page 14 and the final global-Hom assertion; finite open--closed refinement makes the finite-strata induction explicit.
